en.greeting: Hi! Today we learn small words with a big job: a/an, the, and this, that, these, those. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: a or an?
steps.text: Indonesian can say 'Saya punya mobil'. English needs one more word. Let's see it.
steps.body: One countable thing needs a small word in front: **a**, **an**, **my**, **this**, **the** … So: **I have a car**, not 'I have car'. Choose by the first **sound**: **an** before a vowel sound (*an egg, an hour*), **a** before a consonant sound (*a book, a university*). With two or more, use **-s** and no a/an: *two cars*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Check two things: is there an article, and is it a or an?

question.explanation: One job, so we need **a/an**. **Office** starts with a vowel sound, so it's **an office worker**.

steps.title: the: we know which one
steps.text: Now the word **the**. It means: you and I know which one.
steps.body: Use **the** when 1) you said it before (first **a**, then **the**), 2) there is **only one** (*the sun, the moon, the sky*), or 3) it's clear in the place (*Please close **the** door.*). Indonesian **-nya** often does the same job: *pintunya* = **the door**.

steps.title: First a, then the
steps.text: Look at how a changes to the in the second sentence.
steps.body: The first time, the listener doesn't know the thing yet: **a**. After that, they know it: **the**.

examples.en: Budi has a car. The car is red.
We have a new teacher. The teacher is from Medan.
examples.id: Kami punya guru baru. Gurunya dari Medan.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina says: 'I have a cat and a dog.' Now you know the animals, so use **the**.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kucingnya hitam dan anjingnya putih.
question.solution: The cat is black and the dog is white.
question.explanation: Rina said **a cat** and **a dog** before. Now we know which ones, so it's **the cat** and **the dog**.

steps.title: this, that, these, those
steps.text: Now let's point at things.
steps.body: **Near** you: **this** (one) and **these** (two or more) = *ini*. **Far** from you: **that** (one) and **those** (two or more) = *itu*. The word goes **before** the noun: *buku ini* = **this book**. Plural noun → plural word: **these books**, not 'this books'.

steps.title: Near and far
steps.text: Imagine you are at a market in Bandung. Read them out loud.
steps.body: Ask two questions: near or far? One or many?

examples.en: Is this your phone? — Yes, it is.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Near or far? One or many?

question.prompt: You point at some houses far away on a hill. ___ houses are very old.
question.explanation: The houses are **far** and there are **many**, so it's **those**. **That** is for one thing, and **these** is for things near you.

steps.title: Build the question
steps.text: Some keys are on a table across the room. Ask your friend about them.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Apakah itu kunci-kuncimu?
question.explanation: The keys are **far** and there are **many**: **those**. In a question with be, **are** comes first.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards. Say the meaning before you check.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

Listen to the sound: **an engineer**, **an hour**, but **a university**.

steps.title: Watch and read
steps.text: Want more? Watch a short video about this, that, these and those, and read a simple page about a, an and the.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita belajar kata-kata kecil dengan tugas besar: a/an, the, serta this, that, these, those. Yuk, pelan-pelan.

steps.title: a atau an?
steps.text: Bahasa Indonesia bisa bilang 'Saya punya mobil'. Bahasa Inggris butuh satu kata lagi. Yuk lihat.
steps.body: Satu benda yang bisa dihitung butuh kata kecil di depannya: **a**, **an**, **my**, **this**, **the** … Jadi: **I have a car**, bukan 'I have car'. Pilih berdasarkan **bunyi** pertama: **an** sebelum bunyi vokal (*an egg, an hour*), **a** sebelum bunyi konsonan (*a book, a university*). Kalau dua atau lebih, pakai **-s** tanpa a/an: *two cars*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Cek dua hal: ada artikelnya atau tidak, dan a atau an?

question.explanation: Satu pekerjaan, jadi butuh **a/an**. **Office** diawali bunyi vokal, jadi **an office worker**.

steps.title: the: kita tahu yang mana
steps.text: Sekarang kata **the**. Artinya: kamu dan aku tahu yang mana.
steps.body: Pakai **the** kalau 1) sudah disebut sebelumnya (pertama **a**, lalu **the**), 2) hanya ada **satu** (*the sun, the moon, the sky*), atau 3) jelas yang mana di tempat itu (*Please close **the** door.*). Dalam bahasa Indonesia, **-nya** sering punya fungsi yang sama: *pintunya* = **the door**.

steps.title: Pertama a, lalu the
steps.text: Lihat bagaimana a berubah jadi the di kalimat kedua.
steps.body: Pertama kali, pendengar belum tahu bendanya: **a**. Setelah itu, mereka sudah tahu: **the**.

examples.en: Budi has a car. The car is red.
We have a new teacher. The teacher is from Medan.
examples.id: Kami punya guru baru. Gurunya dari Medan.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Rina bilang: 'I have a cat and a dog.' Sekarang kamu sudah tahu hewannya, jadi pakai **the**.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kucingnya hitam dan anjingnya putih.
question.solution: The cat is black and the dog is white.
question.explanation: Rina sudah menyebut **a cat** dan **a dog**. Sekarang kita tahu yang mana, jadi **the cat** dan **the dog**.

steps.title: this, that, these, those
steps.text: Sekarang kita menunjuk benda.
steps.body: **Dekat** denganmu: **this** (satu) dan **these** (dua atau lebih) = *ini*. **Jauh** darimu: **that** (satu) dan **those** (dua atau lebih) = *itu*. Katanya ada **sebelum** kata benda: *buku ini* = **this book**. Kata benda jamak → kata penunjuk jamak: **these books**, bukan 'this books'.

steps.title: Dekat dan jauh
steps.text: Bayangkan kamu di pasar di Bandung. Baca dengan suara keras.
steps.body: Tanyakan dua hal: dekat atau jauh? Satu atau banyak?

examples.en: Is this your phone? — Yes, it is.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dekat atau jauh? Satu atau banyak?

question.prompt: Kamu menunjuk beberapa rumah yang jauh di atas bukit. ___ houses are very old.
question.explanation: Rumahnya **jauh** dan jumlahnya **banyak**, jadi **those**. **That** untuk satu benda, dan **these** untuk benda yang dekat.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaannya
steps.text: Ada beberapa kunci di meja di seberang ruangan. Tanyakan kepada temanmu.

question.explanation: Kuncinya **jauh** dan jumlahnya **banyak**: **those**. Dalam pertanyaan dengan be, **are** ada di depan.

steps.title: Ulang cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya. Sebutkan artinya sebelum kamu cek.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · a/an, the, this/that
artifact.intro: Kata kecil mana yang ada sebelum kata benda?
rows: sudah disebut, hanya satu, atau jelas yang mana
tips: Satu benda yang bisa dihitung tidak boleh berdiri sendiri: **I have a car**, bukan 'I have car'.
Dengarkan bunyinya: **an engineer**, **an hour**, tapi **a university**.
Kata benda jamak → **these/those**: **these books**, bukan 'this books'.

examples.en: Budi has a car. The car is red.

steps.title: Tonton dan baca
steps.text: Mau lebih? Tonton video singkat tentang this, that, these dan those, dan baca halaman sederhana tentang a, an dan the.
